1	Large Language Models (LLMs) with Chain-of-Thought (CoT) reasoning can self-jailbreak: their extended reasoning traces sometimes transition from safe deliberation to committed generation of harmful content. Detecting the precise moment of this safety commitment is essential for real-time intervention, yet no prior work has systematically compared hidden-state (HS) probes against text-based monitors for this task under controlled conditions. We present the first cross-model evaluation of temporal probing methods for safety commitment detection. Our study spans three reasoning models (DeepSeek-R1 8B/32B, QwQ-32B) across two architectures and two scales, and compares HS probes, text monitors, temporal windowing, Gated Recurrent Unit (GRU) sequence models, and geometric baselines including Mahalanobis distance, Bayesian Online Change Point Detection, and Cumulative Sum (CUSUM). Our results reveal three findings. First, temporal context is the dominant factor: expanding the observation window from 1 to 25 reasoning steps improves precision by 12.9 percentage points and reduces false positive rate (FPR) across all models and modalities. Second, the modality advantage is model-dependent: on R1-8B, HS probes Pareto-dominate text probes (+22.4pp precision, $p{<}0.001$; +8.2pp accuracy, $p{=}0.005$; both surviving Bonferroni correction), while on 32B models it ranges from directional (R1-32B, $p{=}0.080$) to absent (QwQ-32B, $p{=}0.828$), with no result surviving Bonferroni correction. Third, geometric distance methods and cross-model transfer fail entirely, and change-point methods (BOCPD, CUSUM) do not improve early detection despite high coverage, defining clear boundaries of current approaches. 1	\section{Problem Setup and Methods}
2	\label{sec:method}
3	
4	\subsection{Safety Commitment Point}
5	\label{sec:commitment-point}
6	
7	When a reasoning model is jailbroken, its CoT transitions from safety-aware deliberation to committed harmful generation. We define the \textbf{Safety Commitment Point} (CP) as the first step after which safety reasoning permanently ceases. We operationalize this on HarmThoughts~\cite{harmthoughts} traces: the CP is the earliest step $t^*$ such that no subsequent step contains safety reasoning. Steps before CP are \emph{pre-commitment}; steps after are \emph{post-commitment}.
8	
9	\subsection{Metrics}
10	\label{sec:metrics}
11	
12	Let $s_t$ denote the probe score at step $t$, $\tau$ the threshold, and $t^*$ the annotated CP.
13	
14	\textbf{Coverage}: fraction of jailbreak traces where any step exceeds $\tau$. \textbf{Pre-CP FPR}: we report both step-level (pooling all pre-CP steps) and trace-level (mean per-trace FPR, treating each trace as an independent observation for paired statistical comparison). \textbf{Precision}: fraction of threshold-exceeding steps that are post-CP. \textbf{Lead time}: steps between first detection and CP ($t^* - t_{\text{detect}}$).
15	
16	All modality comparisons use a two-sided paired permutation test (1000 resamples) on trace-level values, with Bonferroni correction ($\alpha{=}0.017$, 3 models). We use detection criterion $K{=}1$ (single crossing) throughout.
17	
18	\subsection{Models and Data}
19	\label{sec:models-data}
20	
21	We study three models spanning two architectures and two scales:
22	
23	\begin{table}[t]
24	\centering
25	\small
26	\begin{tabular}{lcccccc}
27	\toprule
28	\textbf{Model} & \textbf{Arch.} & \textbf{Params} & \textbf{Layers} & \textbf{Hidden} & \textbf{Traces} & \textbf{Test} \\
29	\midrule
30	R1-8B & Llama & 8B & 32 & 4096 & 209 & 43 \\
31	R1-32B & Qwen & 32B & 64 & 5120 & 100 & 20 \\

33	\bottomrule

36	\label{tab:models}
37	\end{table}

39	R1-8B and R1-32B are distilled from DeepSeek-R1~\citep{deepseekr1}; QwQ-32B~\citep{qwq} is a native reasoning model. Data comes from HarmThoughts~\cite{harmthoughts} with step-level CP annotations. The 32B test sets ($n{=}19$--$20$) provide limited statistical power, partially explaining why neither 32B comparison survives Bonferroni correction.
40	
41	\subsection{Detection Methods}
42	\label{sec:detection-methods}
43	
44	\paragraph{Hidden-state (HS) probes.} At each step, we extract the last-token hidden state from a selected layer and train L2-regularized logistic regression (balanced class weights) on pre-CP vs.\ post-CP labels. Layer selection uses the product of balanced accuracy and crossing rate on the validation set; best layers: R1-8B layer 14 (44\% depth), R1-32B layer 10 (16\%), QwQ-32B layer 2 (3\%).
45	
46	\paragraph{Text probes.} We encode each step's text with all-MiniLM-L6-v2 (384-d sentence embeddings) and apply the same logistic regression procedure. This represents detection performance from surface-level signals alone.
47	
48	\paragraph{Temporal windowing.} For window size $W$, we concatenate features from steps $[t{-}W{+}1, \ldots, t]$ into a single input. We evaluate $W \in \{1, 3, 5, 10, 15, 20, 25\}$, selecting the operating-point $W$ per-model on the validation set.
49	
50	\paragraph{GRU sequence models.} We train GRU classifiers on full step sequences in single-layer (best layer) and multi-layer (7 layers concatenated) variants. Details in \cref{app:gru_details}.
51	
52	\paragraph{Training procedure.} We train with Adam (learning rate $1 \times 10^{-3}$, default $\beta_1{=}0.9$, $\beta_2{=}0.999$), batch size 16, maximum 50 epochs with early stopping (patience 10). Inputs are z-score normalized per dimension.
53	
54	\subsection{Baselines}
55	\label{sec:baselines}
56	
57	\textbf{BOCPD}~\citep{adams2007bayesian}: applied to probe score sequences to test whether commitment produces an abrupt distributional shift. \textbf{CUSUM}: parametric sequential detection accumulating evidence for a mean shift, with configurations $(\delta, h)$ swept in \cref{app:bocpd_config}. \textbf{Mahalanobis distance}: following TrajGuard~\citep{trajguard}, computes geometric separation between pre- and post-CP hidden states. \textbf{Position-only baseline}: predicts ``unsafe'' based solely on step index, testing whether probes capture signal beyond positional correlations.
58

1	\section{Experiments}
2	\label{sec:experiments}
3	
4	We evaluate contrastive trace probes across three reasoning models (R1-8B, R1-32B, QwQ-32B), two signal modalities (hidden states and text), and multiple temporal aggregation strategies. 5	
6	\subsection{Temporal Context as Primary Factor}
7	\label{sec:temporal_primary}
8	
9	The most consistent finding across all experimental conditions is that temporal context improves probe precision and reduces FPR, regardless of signal modality. \cref{fig:window_ablation} shows this pattern for R1-8B; precision and FPR gains hold across all three models, though balanced accuracy improvement is model-dependent.

Under stricter criteria ($K{=}5$, requiring consecutive crossings), larger $W$ can improve effective coverage by eliminating transient false crossings. The transition toward unsafe reasoning is gradual rather than abrupt, so change-point methods cannot exploit discontinuities for early warning. 204	\section{M002 Bug Disclosure}
205	\label{app:bug}
206	
207	We disclose a bug discovered during development that affected intermediate results for QwQ-32B.
208	
209	\paragraph{Issue.} In experiment M002 (text baseline evaluation), the QwQ-32B text probe was inadvertently initialized with a midpoint heuristic placeholder rather than true sentence embeddings from all-MiniLM-L6-v2. Specifically, the placeholder assigned each step a feature vector equal to the midpoint between the mean safe and mean unsafe embeddings from the training set, with small Gaussian noise added. This made the text probe trivially predictive, producing a spuriously significant result ($p{=}0.001$ for HS vs. text FPR difference).
210	
211	\paragraph{Discovery and correction.} The bug was identified during a systematic audit of the feature extraction pipeline. After correction (using actual sentence embeddings), QwQ-32B shows no meaningful modality difference: accuracy $p{=}0.828$, precision $p{=}0.346$, FPR $p{=}0.430$ (two-sided permutation test, 1000 resamples). Full results are reported in \cref{tab:hs_vs_text}.
212	
213	\paragraph{Impact on reported results.} All numbers reported in this paper use the corrected pipeline. No figures, tables, or claims in the main text are affected by the original bug. The correction changed only QwQ-32B text baseline numbers, which now show no significant difference from the HS probe on that model.
214	
215	\paragraph{Commitment to transparency.} We report this bug to maintain scientific integrity. All code, including the git history showing the bug and its fix, will be released with the camera-ready version. Researchers reproducing our results can verify the correction independently.

\section{GRU Training Details}
\label{app:gru_details}

\paragraph{Architecture.} We evaluate two GRU variants. The single-layer variant uses a GRU with hidden dimension 256, taking per-step hidden states from the best layer (selected by accuracy-weighted layer selection) as input. The multi-layer variant concatenates hidden states from 7 layers (evenly spaced through the network) at each step, producing a higher-dimensional input to the same GRU architecture.

\paragraph{Training procedure.} We train with Adam (learning rate $1 \times 10^{-3}$, default $\beta_1{=}0.9$, $\beta_2{=}0.999$), batch size 16, for a maximum of 50 epochs. Early stopping halts training when validation loss does not improve for 10 consecutive epochs. Input features are z-score normalized per dimension using training set statistics.

\paragraph{Evaluation.} We report crossing accuracy (the sustained accuracy at which the probe first exceeds chance for 5 consecutive steps) and detection lead (steps before CP at crossing point). All experiments use 3 random seeds; we report mean $\pm$ standard deviation.

\section{Control Task Methodology}
\label{app:control}

We follow the selectivity framework of \cite{hewitt2019control} to verify that our probes capture genuine safety-relevant structure rather than surface-level correlations.

\paragraph{Procedure.} For each model, we randomly permute the binary labels (pre-CP vs. post-CP) across all steps while preserving the marginal label distribution. We then retrain the probe with identical architecture (L2-regularized logistic regression) and hyperparameters on these shuffled labels. Selectivity is defined as:
\begin{equation}
    \text{Selectivity} = \text{Acc}_{\text{linguistic}} - \text{Acc}_{\text{control}}
\end{equation}
where $\text{Acc}_{\text{linguistic}}$ is the probe accuracy on true labels and $\text{Acc}_{\text{control}}$ is the accuracy on permuted labels. A selectivity of zero indicates that the probe exploits only non-linguistic features (e.g., position); higher values confirm that the representation encodes task-relevant information.

\paragraph{Results.} We repeat the control experiment 5 times with different random permutations and report the mean control accuracy. Selectivity scores are: R1-8B 12.5pp (layer 14), QwQ-32B 15.3pp (layer 2), R1-32B 7.5pp (layer 10). All values exceed the 5pp threshold recommended by \cite{hewitt2019control}. R1-32B's weaker selectivity (7.5pp, near the threshold) is consistent with its overall weaker hidden-state signal. On QwQ-32B, the position baseline accuracy (70.6\%) slightly exceeds the HS probe (67.8\%), indicating that layer 2 encodes strong positional information alongside safety-relevant structure.

\paragraph{Position-only baseline.} As a complementary validation, we train a logistic regression classifier using only the normalized step index ($t / T$ where $T$ is the total trace length) as the input feature. This baseline tests whether temporal position alone explains probe performance. On R1-8B, the position-only baseline produces 15.8\% FPR compared to 8.1\% for the HS probe at matched detection rates. The probe's substantially lower FPR confirms that hidden state features carry information beyond what step position provides.

\label{app:bocpd_config}

We sweep hyperparameters for both Bayesian Online Change-Point Detection (BOCPD) and Cumulative Sum (CUSUM) methods applied to the temporal probe score sequences.

\paragraph{BOCPD configurations.} BOCPD models the sequence of probe scores as piecewise-constant segments with Gaussian observation noise. The hazard rate $\lambda$ controls the prior probability of a change-point at each step ($P(\text{change}) = 1/\lambda$).

\paragraph{CUSUM configurations.} CUSUM accumulates evidence for a positive mean shift. The drift parameter $\delta$ sets the minimum shift size to detect, and the threshold $h$ controls the detection boundary.

These results reveal a coverage-timing tradeoff. BOCPD ($\lambda{=}10$) achieves 28pp higher detection rate than simple thresholding (93.0\% vs.\ 65.1\%), but with lower lead (+3.45 vs.\ +4.89 steps). The transition toward unsafe reasoning is gradual rather than abrupt, so change-point methods cannot exploit discontinuities for early warning. When missed detections are costly, BOCPD's coverage advantage justifies its use despite the timing penalty. When early intervention is the priority, simple thresholding provides better lead time.


\section{M002 Bug Disclosure}
\label{app:bug}

We disclose a bug discovered during development that affected intermediate results for QwQ-32B.

\paragraph{Issue.} In experiment M002 (text baseline evaluation), the QwQ-32B text probe was inadvertently initialized with a midpoint heuristic placeholder rather than true sentence embeddings from all-MiniLM-L6-v2. Specifically, the placeholder assigned each step a feature vector equal to the midpoint between the mean safe and mean unsafe embeddings from the training set, with small Gaussian noise added. This made the text probe trivially predictive, producing a spuriously significant result ($p{=}0.001$ for HS vs. text FPR difference).

\paragraph{Discovery and correction.} The bug was identified during a systematic audit of the feature extraction pipeline. After correction (using actual sentence embeddings), QwQ-32B shows no meaningful modality difference: accuracy $p{=}0.828$, precision $p{=}0.346$, FPR $p{=}0.430$ (two-sided permutation test, 1000 resamples). R1-32B shows directional HS advantages (accuracy $p{=}0.080$, precision $p{=}0.050$, FPR $p{=}0.114$) but none survive Bonferroni correction ($\alpha{=}0.017$). Full results are reported in \cref{tab:hs_vs_text}.

\paragraph{Impact on reported results.} All numbers reported in this paper use the corrected pipeline. No figures, tables, or claims in the main text are affected by the original bug. The correction changed only QwQ-32B text baseline numbers, which now show no significant difference from the HS probe on that model.

\paragraph{Commitment to transparency.} We report this bug to maintain scientific integrity. All code, including the git history showing the bug and its fix, will be released with the camera-ready version. Researchers reproducing our results can verify the correction independently.

5. Abstract is overly long and data-heavy

## Reviewer 2 — Round 2 Review

**Paper**: "Temporal Probing for Safety Commitment Detection in Reasoning Models"
**Venue**: EMNLP 2026 ARR (May cycle)

---

## Summary (2-3句)

本文是首个系统比较 hidden-state probes 与 text monitors 在 reasoning model safety commitment detection 上表现的实证研究。核心发现是 temporal context（观察窗口大小）对检测质量的贡献大于信号模态选择，且 HS probe 优势是 model-dependent 的（仅在 R1-8B 统计显著）。相比 Round 1，论文在标题、Related Work、格式合规、统计方法等方面有实质改善，但 novelty ceiling 和 statistical power 问题仍是主要限制。

---

## Strengths

**S1. 实验设计严谨，统计方法规范。** Bonferroni correction、paired permutation tests、bootstrap CIs、per-seed breakdowns 一应俱全。对非显著结果的谨慎解读（"cannot be interpreted as evidence of absence"，Limitations §1）体现了良好的统计素养。

**S2. Temporal > modality 的核心 finding 有说服力。** Table 2 + Figure 2 + Appendix Table 3 + Appendix Table 4（text window ablation）形成完整的证据链。文本 probes 从 temporal context 获益更大（+12.0pp accuracy vs +3.2pp for HS）这一点特别有力地支撑了"bottleneck is temporal"的 claim。

**S3. Negative results 有信息量且诚实。** TrajGuard 的 Mahalanobis distance 失效（d=6.64-6.73 indistinguishable，Table 5）、BOCPD 的 coverage-timing tradeoff、cross-model transfer 全面失败——这些结果对后续研究有实际导向价值，不是 trivial 的"方法 X 不 work"。

**S4. Control task validation 和 position baseline 设计合理。** 用 Hewitt & Liang (2019) 框架验证 selectivity，额外加 position-only baseline，且诚实报告 QwQ-32B position baseline 略优于 HS probe 的不利结果（Section 5.4），显示科学诚信。

**S5. Bug disclosure (Appendix F) 体现透明度。** 主动披露 M002 bug 及其对 QwQ-32B 结果的影响，在 ML 论文中罕见且值得肯定。

**S6. Related Work 组织清晰。** 6 个 paragraph 主题分明（Probing / Causal / HS Safety / Reasoning Safety / PRM / Cross-Model），每段末尾明确 positioning 本文位置，不是论文堆砌。

---

## Weaknesses

**W1 [warning] Abstract 过长且数据堆砌，不符合 150-250 word 惯例。**
- 具体位置：sections/abstract.tex
- 问题：Abstract 约 280-300 words（远超典型 EMNLP paper 的 200 word 甜点），大量堆砌具体数字（+12.9pp, +22.4pp, p<0.001, +8.2pp, p=0.005, p=0.080, p=0.828, 93%, +31 steps, 85.5%）。审稿人在 30 秒内难以提取核心 insight。
- 建议：保留"temporal > modality"和"model-dependent"两个核心 finding 各用 1 个代表性数字，删除 Bonferroni、BOCPD、CUSUM 等细节，控制在 200 words 以内。Abstract 不是 Results 的缩写。

**W2 [warning] 核心贡献的 novelty ceiling：empirical comparison without methodological contribution。**
- 具体位置：Introduction contribution list (items 1-3)
- 问题：三个贡献均为 empirical observations（temporal context matters, modality is model-dependent, negative results）。论文未提出新的检测方法、新的理论框架或新的数据集。对 EMNLP main track 而言，一篇纯 benchmarking + negative results 的论文需要更强的"so what"——读完后 practitioner 应该做什么不同的事情？目前的 deployment recommendation（Section 6 最后一段："start with temporal windowing, then evaluate modality per model"）过于直觉化，缺乏 novelty。
- 为什么影响评分：EMNLP 的 Excitement 维度要求论文不只是 informative，还要 exciting。当 takeaway 是"加大窗口、per-model 调参"，excitement 有限。
- 建议：考虑是否能将 temporal windowing 形式化为一种新方法（而非仅仅是 concatenation），或提出 adaptive window selection 策略作为 actionable contribution。

**W3 [warning] Statistical power 不足削弱 Contribution 2。**
- 具体位置：Table 1 (n=20, n=19 for 32B models), Section 5.2, Limitations §1
- 问题：Contribution 2 声称"modality advantage is model-dependent"，但 32B 的 non-significant results 可能纯粹因为 power 不足（n≈20，Cohen's d<0.5 不可检测）。这意味着"model-dependent"的 claim 同样可以解读为"underpowered"。论文在 Limitations 中承认了这一点（"cannot be interpreted as evidence of absence"），但在 Abstract/Introduction/Conclusion 中仍将其作为核心贡献宣传，存在 overclaim 风险。
- 建议：在 Abstract 和 Introduction 中明确 qualify 这是"tentative evidence"而非 definitive finding for 32B models。

**W4 [warning] Architecture/scale/distillation 三重 confound 未充分讨论。**
- 具体位置：Limitations §6, Discussion ¶2
- 问题：R1-8B 是唯一的 Llama 架构、唯一的 8B 模型、唯一的 distilled model。HS probe 优势可能来自 (a) Llama vs Qwen 架构差异, (b) 8B vs 32B scale, (c) distillation vs native reasoning，或三者的交互。论文在 Discussion 中猜测"distillation compresses safety signal"但无证据。Limitations §6 提到 confound 但仅占 3 行。
- 建议：这是论文最核心的 confound，应该在 Discussion 中有一个独立 paragraph 系统讨论三种 alternative explanations 和可能的 disambiguation 方案（e.g., 测试 Llama-3 70B native model 或 Qwen-2.5 7B distilled model）。

**W5 [warning] High FPR on safe traces (39-62%) 与 deployment framing 矛盾。**
- 具体位置：Limitations §5, Discussion ¶3 ("Deployment implications"), Conclusion ¶4
- 问题：Limitations 中承认所有方法在纯 safe traces 上 FPR 为 39-62%，但 Discussion 和 Conclusion 仍然用 "deployment recommendations" 的 framing 给出实践建议。一个 FPR 40%+ 的系统在任何生产环境中都不可用。这种 framing gap 会让审稿人感到 disconnect。
- 建议：将 "deployment recommendations" 改为 "design guidelines for future monitoring systems" 或类似措辞，明确当前方法是 diagnostic tool 而非 production-ready。
